issue.standard_remedy: Consolidate tail suppliers into preferred suppliers
issue.summary: 28 of 70 suppliers share the last 20% of category spend

plan.diagnosis: The IT services & software category exhibits severe fragmentation with an HHI of 195 (well below the 1500 threshold for healthy concentration) and 28 tail suppliers generating only 1,531,079 USD across 20% of the 7,785,568 USD total category spend. The top supplier holds only 4.4% share, indicating no strategic partnerships exist and procurement is highly transactional, driving excess administrative costs and limiting leverage.

remedy_steps.step: Conduct tail supplier spend analysis to identify the 28 suppliers in scope, map their services to preferred supplier capabilities, and classify by migration difficulty (low/medium/high complexity)

Issue RFP to top 5 existing suppliers including Monterrey Continental Components Corp. to negotiate volume commitment discounts (target 8-12% reduction) and expanded scope to absorb tail supplier volumes
remedy_steps.owner: Sourcing Lead with Procurement Director approval

remedy_steps.step: Execute supplier consolidation: award contracts to 2-3 preferred suppliers, communicate transition plan to business stakeholders, and establish 90-day migration timeline for low-complexity tail suppliers (target 60% of tail spend)
remedy_steps.owner: Category Manager with IT stakeholder alignment

remedy_steps.step: Implement ERP controls across all platforms to restrict procurement to approved supplier list and route exceptions through Category Manager approval workflow
remedy_steps.owner: ERP Systems Administrator with Procurement Systems team

remedy_steps.step: Migrate remaining medium-complexity tail suppliers (target additional 30% of tail spend) and establish quarterly business reviews with preferred suppliers to track SLA compliance and innovation opportunities

plan.expected_impact: Consolidating 28 tail suppliers representing 1,531,079 USD will yield estimated savings of 122,486 USD annually (8% price reduction on migrated spend) plus 45,000 USD in reduced administrative costs from fewer supplier relationships.
kpis: Number of active IT services suppliers reduced from 70 to 42 (40% reduction)
Tail spend reduced from 1,531,079 USD to under 459,324 USD (70% reduction)
Category HHI increased from 195 to above 800
Savings realization of 167,486 USD (10.9% of tail spend)
Preferred supplier share increased to minimum 60% of category spend
risks: Business unit resistance to change from incumbent tail suppliers may delay migration and require executive sponsorship
Service quality degradation if preferred suppliers lack niche capabilities currently provided by tail suppliers
Preferred suppliers may lack capacity to absorb 1,531,079 USD in additional volume within 90-day timeline
Multi-ERP environment complexity may cause inconsistent supplier master data and control implementation gaps across SAP, Oracle EBS, Dynamics 365, NetSuite, and Coupa
erp_actions: SAP: Set deletion flag (LOEVM) in LFA1 for 28 tail suppliers after migration; update source lists (EORD) to restrict IT services category to approved suppliers only; configure release strategy (ME28) for non-preferred supplier POs over 5,000 USD threshold

Oracle EBS: Disable 28 tail supplier sites in PO_VENDOR_SITES_ALL after final invoice processing; create approved supplier list (ASL) entries for preferred suppliers with category assignments; implement sourcing rules to default preferred suppliers
Dynamics 365: Inactivate tail vendor records post-migration; configure procurement policies to require approval workflow for non-preferred vendors in IT services procurement category
NetSuite: Set tail vendor records to inactive status; update preferred vendor lists on item records for IT services category; enable approval routing for purchases from non-preferred vendors

Coupa: Remove tail suppliers from commodity assignments for IT services category; update supplier segmentation to 'Tactical - Phase Out'; enable pre-approval requirement for requisitions outside approved supplier list
